transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-15
- Time: 14:30 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortega (BlueFjord VP Eng), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Samir Khan (Platform Eng), Lena Zhou (Security), Mia Park (FinOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
A quick QBR-style checkin to align on governance and capacity retrofit for BlueFjord's inference workloads. Discussed Dedicated pools, private deployment constraints, KV cache behavior for long-context prompts, and next steps toward a pilot.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll go ~40 minutes. Quick agenda — usage and cost trends, security questions, and pilot scope. Marcus will run through perf notes.
00:28 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Thanks, Aisha. We just came out of a retail campaign last month; saw spikes — latency jitter during the middle of day. Cost was higher than expected. Hoping to nail down a plan so Finance doesn't faint.
00:46 Speaker 3 (Mia): yep, the burn surprised us. Wanted to understand where tokens are coming from and if caching or batching will help.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Totally. Marcus, can you take the perf/architecture part?
01:12 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Sure. So, BlueFjord — based on the trace you gave last quarter, typical request sizes are 1.2k tokens median with a tail to 8k. The big wins are prefix caching for conversational reuse and aggressive batching for background scoring. We recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscaling buffer.
01:35 Speaker 5 (Priya): Quick question — when you say prefix caching, are you talking about KV cache — like that internal thing we tried to script? Because our internal cache invalidation made things weird last time.
01:50 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Yeah KV cache — sometimes the invalidation rules are conservative. With Redwood, the runtime exposes cache controls — you can set TTLs per route and version pinning so cache invalidations don't cause cold starts. Note: the transcription might show "K V cache" sometimes.
02:12 Speaker 3 (Samir): Are there differences between hosted and dedicated for cache behavior?
02:19 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Functionally same, but Dedicated gives you pinned GPUs so cache warm-ups are faster and more predictable. Hosted can evict under high multi-tenant churn.
02:40 Speaker 6 (Lena): On security — we need to validate that logs, audit trails, and key management meet our infosec policy. HSM/KMS integration notes?
02:54 Speaker 4 (Marcus): For Private or Dedicated with VPC peering, we offer customer KMS integration and optional HSM-backed keys for model keys and audit log signing. We'll send the security pack.
03:10 Speaker 6 (Lena): Great. Also need retention windows for logs and the ability to flag redactions. We have PCI-adjacent data flows.
03:22 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Put another way — if we go Dedicated, can we get SLA latency targets for peak 95th perc?
03:32 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Yes, we can commit to SLOs in the Dedicated contract. Example: 95th token latency of Xms for the 4k path — we'll run a targeted benchmark with your prompt set.
03:46 Speaker 5 (Priya): What's the benchmarking cadence? We need to ensure model rollouts don't regress.
03:52 Speaker 1 (Aisha): We do canary rollouts and have perf dashboards in Console. Marcus will share sample dashboards and a microbench.
04:05 Speaker 4 (Marcus): I'll run the microbench against your top-10 prompts; include cold-start and warm-cache paths. Also include quantized variants — sometimes 4-bit q can reduce cost without big quality loss.
04:25 Speaker 3 (Samir): Regarding private deployments — how invasive is the on-prem package? We don't want to re-architect network flows.
04:33 Speaker 4 (Marcus): The on-prem option is a containerized runtime with a light-weight control plane; it needs a small set of ports and a KMS endpoint. We provide a deployment guide. There are slight infra changes but we try to keep the control-plane footprint small.
04:55 Speaker 5 (Priya): Can Redwood help with the model variant routing? We want lower-cost variants for low-risk features and high-quality models for core flows.
05:05 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Yes — runtime supports policy-based routing. You can tag routes and set fallback chains. We'll show a sample policy during the pilot.
05:20 Speaker 7 (Mia): cost question — if we move to Dedicated, how does billing work for idle capacity? We have spiky usage and not a lot of overnight traffic.
05:31 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Dedicated has reserved commitments with burst capacity. We can structure monthly commits and a buffer for bursts. Also Redwood Optimize suggestions can reduce unit cost via batching and caching.
05:44 Speaker 3 (Samir): Any quick wins to lower QPS cost without a big infra change?
05:50 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Short term — implement prefix caching and lower sequence-length of assistant responses where acceptable, use response truncation, and enable async background ranking outside SLO paths. That can cut effective tokens by ~20-35% for many apps.
06:12 Speaker 2 (Daniel): On governance — we need per-team RBAC, model pinning controls, and audit exports for compliance.
06:21 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Console supports route-level RBAC and audit logs. Exports can be pushed to S3 or to your SIEM with timestamped entries. We'll share the docs link: https://redwood.example/security-pack (note: auto-transcript sometimes munges URLs).
06:45 Speaker 6 (Lena): We'll verify retention and PHI redaction capabilities. Also want to confirm that the Dedicated pool can be isolated per business unit.
06:58 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Yes, we can create separate pools and scopes.
07:10 Speaker 5 (Priya): On pilot success criteria — what if we define latency < 300ms p95 for 1-2k median prompts and cost per 1k tokens below target X?
07:24 Speaker 1 (Aisha): That sounds reasonable; we'll formalize metrics. Marcus, can we get baseline numbers by EOD Tue?
07:31 Speaker 4 (Marcus): I'll try. Need the prompt set and 72-hour trace to make it accurate.
07:40 Speaker 2 (Daniel): We'll push that this week.
07:46 Speaker 7 (Mia): Finance wants an estimate for three scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated small commit, and dedicated annual commit.
07:56 Speaker 1 (Aisha): We'll include that in the pricing sheet.
08:05 Speaker 5 (Priya): Quick technical deep dive — caching heuristics: what happens when conversation state changes often and prefix reuse is low?
08:16 Speaker 4 (Marcus): If prefix reuse is low, caching helps less — then batching and smaller model variants are most effective. Also consider dynamic reranking where the model generates short candidates and a lightweight ranker does final selection.
08:39 Speaker 3 (Samir): Does Redwood support on-the-fly quantization or just pre-compiled quantized variants?
08:45 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Right now we provide pre-built quantized variants and compilation profiles. On-the-fly is planned but not generally available.
08:56 Speaker 5 (Priya): Good to know.
09:05 Speaker 6 (Lena): About audit logs — can we get real-time alerts for anomalous data exfil patterns?
09:12 Speaker 4 (Marcus): You can stream logs to your SIEM and set rules. Redwood also provides native anomaly flags for unusual token patterns, but we recommend SIEM for enterprise alerts.
09:28 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Any legal/procurement blockers we should preempt?
09:35 Speaker 1 (Aisha): SSO/SAML and standard DPA are usually the items; Lena, do you have specific clauses to flag?
09:42 Speaker 6 (Lena): We need a clause for encrypted-at-rest keys managed by customer KMS and an explicit data residency statement.
09:50 Speaker 1 (Aisha): We'll add that to the contract skeleton.
10:00 Speaker 7 (Mia): On cost savings — give us a conservative and optimistic number?
10:05 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Conservatively 15% with caching and batching; optimistically 35% if you adopt quantized variants for non-core flows and refactor a few long prompts.
10:18 Speaker 5 (Priya): Benchmarks — do you have side-by-side quality evals for the quantized models vs fp16? We need to present to Product.
10:26 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Yes, we'll include eval diffs and a qualitative rubric. We'll also capture prompt-critical failure modes.
10:38 Speaker 2 (Daniel): On timeline — we'd like pilot done before Black Friday spike, ideally full rollout by late November. Is that feasible?
10:49 Speaker 1 (Aisha): It's tight but doable if we start pilot in the next two weeks and keep scope focused.
11:00 Speaker 5 (Priya): What's the pilot scope you recommend?
11:06 Speaker 4 (Marcus): 2-week pilot: 1) run microbench with your prompt set, 2) deploy Dedicated small pool with warm cache for a subset of routes, 3) collect metrics (latency p95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens), 4) security sign-off on audit logs and KMS.
11:29 Speaker 3 (Samir): We'll need a rollback plan — if latency regresses on rollout.
11:35 Speaker 4 (Marcus): Rollback is route-based and we keep previous version pinned. Canary at 10% then 50% then 100%.
11:45 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Great. Any other blockers?
11:50 Speaker 6 (Lena): Need to review SOC2 artifacts and potentially sign an NDA extension.
11:56 Speaker 1 (Aisha): We'll include SOC2 docs and the SLA draft in the materials.
12:05 Speaker 7 (Mia): Finance note — will the pilot be billable?
12:10 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Typically pilot includes usage billing; for enterprise pilots we sometimes credit a portion depending on contract. We'll put options in the sheet.
12:22 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Okay let's recap next steps.
12:28 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Recap: Redwood sends pricing + security pack + perf microbench. BlueFjord sends prompt set and trace. Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 10/26. Action items in calendar invite.
12:50 Speaker 4 (Marcus): I'll attach a baseline perf CSV and a short runbook.
13:05 Speaker 5 (Priya): Thanks, everyone.
13:10 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Thanks.
13:12 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Bye all.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 1/2) and dropped punctuation. Some product names may be mis-typed — e.g., Redwood Dedicated sometimes appears as "red wood dedicated".
